content: {"id": "772d8f04-94f7-4eaa-8cfc-8a86f945a5aa", "role": "user", "content": [{"text": "In AWS Config I have a standalone acm-certificate-expiration-check rule with a 14-day threshold, and my conformance pack also includes acm-certificate-expiration-check but with a 90-day threshold. Is the standalone rule just a duplicate I should delete to save on evaluations? No account access required.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
{"id": "f6cc2e10-df97-4398-9bdc-ceba55a14ad3", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "chat_title", "title": "AWS Config duplicate ACM certificate expiration rules"}]}

{"id": "33c48f19-33cf-445a-b0a2-282bbf057745", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Not a true duplicate — those two rules would actually serve different purposes, so deleting the standalone one isn't just a cleanup with no downside. Here's the distinction:

**Why they're not redundant:**
- The rule `acm-certificate-expiration-check` takes `daysToExpiration` as a parameter. A standalone deployment with **14 days** is typically an early-warning/critical-alert threshold — "cert expires very soon, act now."
- The conformance pack's copy with **90 days** is usually the broader compliance/governance threshold — "start tracking renewal well in advance."

These represent two different alerting tiers, not the same check twice. If you delete the standalone 14-day rule, you lose the tighter, more urgent signal and only keep the 90-day warning — which means you'd have far less lead-time visibility right before actual expiration.

**On the cost/evaluation angle:**
- Both rule instances *do* independently evaluate every ACM certificate in scope and each generates its own configuration item evaluation — so yes, you are paying for two evaluations of the same certificates on presumably the same trigger (configuration changes to ACM certs).
- If cost is the primary driver, the better fix usually isn't blanket deletion — it's consolidating to a **single rule with one threshold** (or, if your Config setup supports it, keeping both but confirming they're not both on continuous/high-frequency recording for the same resource type).

**What I'd check before deciding anything (no account access needed to reason about it, but worth confirming when you do have access):**
- Whether the standalone rule and the conformance pack rule are triggered on the same event source (config change vs. periodic) — if one is periodic and one is config-change-triggered, the actual evaluation volume/cost difference may be small.
- Whether anything downstream (dashboards, SNS notifications, remediation actions) is wired specifically to the standalone rule's compliance name — deleting it could silently break those integrations even if the conformance pack rule keeps "the same" logic.

So: don't delete it purely as a "duplicate." If you want, I can walk through your actual Config setup to check evaluation frequency and downstream dependencies on the standalone rule before you decide whether to consolidate.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
